memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
"'These are the LORD's appointed festivals, the sacred assemblies you
are to proclaim at their appointed times: The LORD's Passover begins
at twilight on the fourteenth day of the first month'"
- Lev 23:4-5 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Passover came first in the yearly cycle, and rightly so. It marked the
night God rescued Israel out of Egypt. A lamb was killed, its blood
placed on the doorframes, and the judgment that fell across the land
passed over every home covered by that blood.

Israel was not saved because they were better than the Egyptians. They
were saved because they were under the blood of a lamb.

Dear friend, the New Testament makes the connection explicit. Paul
writes that Christ, our Passover lamb, has been sacrificed (1 Cor 5:7).
John the Baptist pointed at Jesus and said, "Look, the Lamb of God, who
takes away the sin of the world" (John 1:29). And Jesus was crucified
during Passover week itself - not by coincidence, but by design.

This is not a promise still waiting to be fulfilled. It has already
happened. The Lamb has been slain. The blood has been applied. The
judgment has passed over everyone who is in Christ.

Every year Israel remembered a rescue. We remember a greater one. When
you take the bread and the cup, you are standing in a very old story
that found its ending at a cross.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do I still feel the wonder of being rescued, or has it become
   routine?
2. Am I trusting in the Lamb's blood, or in my own record?
3. How can I make remembering the cross a regular practice?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Lord Jesus, You are my Passover Lamb. Thank You that judgment passed
over me because it fell on You. Let me never forget the cost. Amen.
